explanation: Pointing directly at someone or something with your index finger is seen as impolite in Singapore; multiple etiquette guides describe it as rude and recommend gesturing with an open hand or thumb instead. It's a soft social norm rather than a severe taboo, so casual slip-ups are unlikely to cause lasting offense.
local_tip: Gesture with an open hand (palm up) or a nod of the head toward what you mean, instead of pointing your index finger at people.

also_check.note: Pointing with the index finger is seen as impolite; gesturing with an open hand is preferred.
Pointing with the index finger is common and unremarkable in everyday, casual interactions.
Pointing at people with the index finger is considered impolite; the thumb is commonly used instead.
